title: The Last-Over Nervous System: What Pressure Does to Rajasthan Royals Fans
dek: No part of a match tests a fan like the final over. Rajasthan Royals' record in close finishes shows how often the nerves have been rewarded.
excerpt: Rajasthan Royals have played many close finishes, and won more than half. Whether that record reflects skill or luck is the question every nervous fan asks.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Twenty Overs, One Over
body: Close finishes are where fandom is most physical: the last over, the required runs, the field coming in. They are also where results feel least controllable.
The CricField warehouse holds no survey, sentiment or social-media data, so it cannot measure what fans feel. It can measure what they have watched.

sections.heading: The Record in Close Matches
body: Rajasthan Royals have won {{ev:lo-close-won}} of {{ev:lo-close-n}} close matches, {{ev:lo-close-pct}}, against {{ev:lo-other-pct}} in matches that were not close. That ranks them {{ev:lo-close-rank}} of ten franchises.

The ninety-five per cent interval for their close-match win rate is {{ev:lo-close-ci}}. If each close match were a coin toss, a record this far from even would occur with probability {{ev:lo-close-p}}.

sections.heading: Final-Over Chases
body: {{ev:lo-lo}} of Rajasthan Royals' matches were decided by a chase completed in the final over, and RR won {{ev:lo-lw}} of them.
Across the league, the number of franchises whose close-match record differs from a coin toss at the conventional threshold is {{ev:lo-close-sig}}.

sections.heading: Skill or Luck?
body: Close-match records are noisy; a few deliveries decide them. Fans remember the wins and losses as character, but the statistics usually point to chance.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Nerves, Not a Pattern
body: Rajasthan Royals' close-match record is consistent with chance; the nerves are real, but the pattern is not proven.
Measuring what close finishes do to fans would need attendance and engagement data around those matches.

methodology: CricField holds ball-by-ball cricket data and no fan survey, sentiment or social-media data. This article measures the cricket fans have experienced; statements about fans themselves are labelled hypotheses. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Close = decided by ten runs or fewer, six balls or fewer to spare, or a super over. Final-over chase = chasing side won with five or fewer legal balls to spare.
